rows.description: You feel a duty to fulfil family dreams and pay back sacrifice. Gratitude is real, but your life is also yours. Talk honestly about what you can give and want to do, and seek the path where duty and desire overlap.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: admiration, comparison

rows.description: Volunteering, teaching or building something for others gives a sense of use. Start small and consistent, listen to what people need instead of imposing solutions, and avoid service performed for applause.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: admiration, comparison

rows.description: You admire an elder who lived simply and helped many. Ask about their choices and regrets, not just achievements. Legacy is mostly the quiet daily conduct that others remember, not monuments.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: comparison

rows.description: Peers seem to have clear callings and big achievements. Comparison steals your calm. Look at what you find worth working on even when no one is watching; purpose often emerges through doing, not waiting.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: admiration

rows.description: You start thinking about the world you leave to children and juniors, such as climate, honesty and fairness. Pick one area, act locally, and live consistently with it. Small, steady action beats grand declarations.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: admiration, comparison

rows.description: A younger person keeps making mistakes you once made. Remember your own learning curve, explain reasons rather than orders, and let them try safe failures. Mentoring is investing, not proving superiority.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: admiration, dependence, envy, pride

rows.description: Seeing your mentee grow makes you proud, and slightly wistful. Celebrate them without claiming credit, and be glad when they surpass you. Good mentors work towards being no longer needed.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: admiration, dependence, envy

rows.description: A younger colleague looks up to you and copies your habits. It is an honour and a responsibility. Be honest about your failures, model integrity, and do not seek adoration or use their trust for your ego.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: dependence, envy, pride
related mind states: admiration, trust, determination

rows.description: A mentee keeps asking you to decide everything. Help them build judgment: ask what they think, offer options, and celebrate independent choices. Rescuing them each time weakens them and burdens you.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: admiration, envy, pride

rows.description: A talented junior threatens you with faster progress. Notice the sting, then decide: share opportunities, give credit, and keep growing your own skills. Holding them back protects your ego but hurts the team and you.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: admiration, dependence, pride
